deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an archival cover document: a copy ('Abschrift') of a letter by Professor K. Schering, made by his sister-in-law. From the next page she signs as M. Schering, the widow of Ernst Schering. The letter is dated or registered '1897. 4658.' The Göttingen library stamp ('Ex Bibliotheca Regiae Academiae Georgiae Aug.') and the shelf note 'Riemann 36' appear on it.

K. Schering reports on three fascicles he took to inspect. He states they are all written in Ernst Schering's hand, not Riemann's:
(1) two folio sheets stitched together, headed 'Aetherbewegungen I'. This is a draft (Concept) of part of (2).
(2) three stitched folio sheets headed 'Aetherbewegungen II', with several loose inserts. The pencil inserts are probably in another hand.

He says the content of (1) and (2) is closely related to, and partly identical with, pp. 496-502 of Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke, edited by H. Weber (Leipzig 1876). There that material appears among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', i.e. the natural-philosophy fragments on aether motion, gravitation and light. He concludes the subject also remained unfinished with Riemann. He finds it striking that Ernst produced two elaborations. He wonders whether Ernst meant to publish it jointly with Riemann, or whether part of it is Ernst's own independent work; he doubts this can now be decided.

The next page describes the third fascicle, 'Hypothesen der Geometrie', related to the Habilitationsvortrag. It also records M. Schering's remark that her husband did independent research in this area, citing his correspondence with Helmholtz.

There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Provenance statement: the 'Aetherbewegungen I/II' manuscripts in this bundle are in Ernst Schering's handwriting. They are drafts or elaborations corresponding to Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments (Werke 1876, pp. 496-502).
results.modern_name: Archival/provenance note (Riemann Nachlass, Schering's role as early custodian/editor)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely an archival provenance letter with no mathematical content. It is mildly interesting for Nachlass history: it attributes the handwriting of the aether fascicles to Ernst Schering and raises the question of his independent contribution. That is a detail of editorial history, not a mathematical discovery.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Ob er es mit Riemann zusammen herausgeben wollte?': in the image 'es' appears as a superscript insertion above the line ('Ob er ^es^ mit'), and the word read as 'zusammen' is partly struck through or uncertain.
'Fasikel' is as written (a nonstandard spelling of 'Faszikel').
The page also bears the pencil shelf mark 'Riemann 36' at top right and the library stamp 'EX BIBLIOTHECA REGIAE ACADEM. GEORGIAE AUG.'; neither appears in the transcription.
The writer of the copy is the 'Schwägerin' of K. Schering ('meines Schwagers'), i.e. M. Schering, Ernst Schering's widow, who signs on the following page.
